findings.title: The bulk loader writes while ledger strict mode is on
findings.intended: HD-0301 (supported): spec 213's API contract excludes the bulk loader and raw SQL from strict mode; the USER_GUIDE (docs/USER_GUIDE.md:1107-1121) says strict refuses create_node, create_edge 'and the other methods'.
findings.remedy: State the exclusion in the USER_GUIDE next to strict mode (the contract is supported as is).
findings.notes: Behaviour matches the supported contract (HD-0301); the defect is the USER_GUIDE wording. Severity lowered to S3 accordingly.

observed.verdict: loader wrote under strict mode (contract exception; docs say otherwise)
observed.oracle: Spec 213 API contract: bulk loader and raw SQL are outside strict mode (HD-0301)

findings.title: Strict mode reaches another engine only after its five-second cache expires
findings.intended: USER_GUIDE.md:1107-1121 states refusal without a window; HD-1103 (supported): strict mode is a client-side guard whose cache behaviour must be inventoried.
findings.remedy: Document the window and the fail-open rule next to set_strict, or check on the server.

observed.verdict: another engine wrote within its cache window
observed.oracle: once strict is on, every engine refuses the guarded writes

findings.title: A direct edge delete leaves the ledger's live link for the edge
findings.intended: CONTEXT.md:198-205 (no live statement outlives its content); INV-stmt (semantics/writesets.json).
findings.remedy: Route delete_edge (and the Cypher relationship delete) through Eraser.EraseEdges.
findings.notes: The first live attempt (breadth-a-live-ledger, p0303) read ^IVG.Ledger('tuple') with graph key 0 instead of GraphKey.ForLedger('') ($Char(1)) and decided nothing; p0303b corrects the key. A ledger create of the same triple after the direct delete allocated a new statement (p0303: 1 then 2), so the reuse happens through the tuple index for a directly re-created edge, as the finding says.

observed.verdict: statement 4 and its tuple entry stay live after the row is gone; the re-created edge inherits it
observed.oracle: no live statement outlives its edge row (CONTEXT.md:198-205, INV-stmt)

findings.title: Storing an edge over a marked edge does not take the edge over
findings.intended: ADR-0009 (CONTEXT.md:66-73) and HD-0302 (supported): an explicit structural create clears the temporal mark; a temporal-backed row must not delete an explicitly written edge.
findings.remedy: Run the adopt step after store_edge's swallowed duplicate.
findings.notes: Discriminating control in the same probe: over the same marked row, create_edge adopts (qualifiers NULL) and its edge survives the last temporal delete; store_edge keeps {"temporal":true} and its edge is deleted (data loss).

observed.verdict: create_edge's edge survives (control), store_edge's edge is deleted
observed.oracle: an explicitly written edge survives the last temporal delete (ADR-0009, CONTEXT.md:66-73)

findings.title: A bulk write larger than one chunk is not one transaction on the server-loader path
findings.intended: USER_GUIDE.md:238-241: each bulk write is a transaction of its own.
findings.remedy: Run the loader on the cursor's own process inside the WriteTxn (txn.native()), or one loader call per transaction.
findings.notes: from_connect engine: 1,001 of 2,000 nodes committed and visible to a READ COMMITTED reader while the call was stalled in chunk 2; the journal shows two committed node transactions by the engine's Native API process, none by its cursor process. A client killed inside chunk 2 left exactly chunk 1 committed (breadth-a-live-03-bulk-killed-client).

observed.verdict: 1001 of 2000 nodes committed and visible to another process while the call ran; 2 node-writing transactions, pids ['7440'] (cursor pid 7437)
observed.oracle: no other process sees part of one bulk write; its writes are one transaction of the caller's

findings.title: create_node answers False for a write IRIS refuses as invalid
findings.intended: create_node docstring: False means the node already exists; 4.6.0 R203: a refusal is not 'already there'.
findings.remedy: Drop the 'validation failed' match or width-check the graph name.
findings.notes: Also settles premise P-0307 live (a 300-character graph name).

observed.oracle: False means the node already exists (create_node docstring); a refusal raises (R203)

findings.title: The server path of bulk_ingest_edges skips a refused edge without an error
findings.intended: 4.7.0 row 14: every bulk writer raises for a refused row; the SQL path of bulk_ingest_edges raises GraphWriteError.
findings.remedy: Width-check in Python before sending; make the loader throw on a refused row.

observed.verdict: the too-wide edge was dropped, count 1, no error
observed.oracle: a refused row raises (4.7.0 row 14 for every other bulk writer; the SQL path raises)

findings.title: The bulk loader stores a NaN or infinite edge property as JSON no reader accepts
findings.intended: 4.6.0 R307: create_edge and store_edge refuse NaN/Infinity because IRIS JSON functions then fail every relationship read.
findings.notes: create_edge refused the same value (ValueError); the Cypher read of the loaded graph failed with SQLCODE -149 in CY_REL_PROP.

observed.verdict: loader stored NaN and the Cypher read failed
observed.oracle: a stored edge never makes a relationship read fail (R307 refuses NaN on create_edge)

cypher_read:
<SQL ERROR>; Details: [SQLCODE: <-149>:<SQL Function encountered an error>]
[Location: <ServerLoop - Query Fetch>]
[%msg: <SQL Function GRAPH_KG.CY_REL_PROP failed with error:  SQLCODE=-400,%msg=>]

findings.title: The bulk loader rebuilds the indexes of Graph_KG whatever schema it loaded
findings.intended: ADR-0016 / CONTEXT.md:20-24: a namespace's IVG schema may be other than Graph_KG.
findings.remedy: Derive the class names from the schema.
findings.notes: Live check blocked-access: needs a namespace whose IVG Schema is not Graph_KG (namespaces are the orchestrator's). Related observation (breadth-a-live-bulkloader-noindex): edges BulkLoader.load_edges wrote with its default %NOINDEX and no rebuild_all_indices were invisible to indexed reads (0 vs 2 rows) and survived erase_graph of their graph; reported to the erasure lane, not counted here (the loader's docstring requires the rebuild).
findings.observed: rebuild_all_indices calls %BuildIndices on the fixed classes Graph.KG.rdfedges/rdflabels/rdfprops/nodes (iris_vector_graph/bulk_loader.py:495).

findings.title: create_edge's adoption of a marked row runs after its transaction commits
findings.intended: create_edge docstring/ADR-0009: an explicit create over a marked row adopts it in the same write.
findings.remedy: Adopt inside the same transaction as the guarded insert.
findings.notes: New, from the footprint sub-lane's static reading; confirmed in source, not provoked (a narrow interleaving).
findings.observed: When the guarded insert finds the triple, txn.commit() runs first and _adopt_temporal_row's UPDATE runs afterwards as its own statement (iris_vector_graph/_engine/nodes_edges.py:1236-1252); a temporal delete in between removes the marked row and the call answers False (duplicate) with no edge.

findings.title: Property lookups with a limit return a storage-order subset
findings.intended: A capped lookup answers a defined subset (no stated order at the pin; ADR/USER_GUIDE silent).
findings.remedy: ORDER BY the subject (and value) under a limit, or document the arbitrary subset.
findings.notes: New, from the storage-order disposition (the coordinator's scan missed both: TOP is built in a separate string).
findings.observed: get_node_ids_by_property and get_property_pairs_like build SELECT TOP n ... with no ORDER BY (iris_vector_graph/_engine/nodes_edges.py:820, 904): with a limit the caller gets the first n rows in scan order.
